questions.q: What do doing nothing and doing everything have in common, per McKeown?
a: Both are signs of learned helplessness
Both lead to faster progress
Both require careful planning
Both show strong personal boundaries
questions.why: Lesson 1 says both camps give up the power to choose.

questions.q: What did Seligman's dog experiment demonstrate?
a: Dogs that could not stop shocks stopped trying to escape
Dogs that could stop shocks became more fearful
All the dogs eventually escaped the box
Older dogs learned the lever faster
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes dogs that had learned to accept their fate.

questions.q: How much buffer does McKeown recommend when planning a task?
a: Add 50 percent more time than you estimate
Double the time you think it will take
Add exactly fifteen minutes to every task
Plan only half of what you think you can do
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to add half the estimated time for the unexpected.

questions.q: How does the summary describe an editor's job, citing Jack Dorsey?
a: Mostly removing what does not add value
Mostly adding new projects and ideas
Mostly delegating work to others
Mostly measuring results and sales
questions.why: Lesson 2 says editing is about adding, but mostly about removing.
